title: How emperors and officials were blamed for natural disasters in ancient China
description: Political resignations are often presented as expressions of accountability after public disasters. Yet the departure of a senior official does not necessarily mean that the individual was personally responsible for what happened. Recent events in Hong Kong and Spain illustrate the distinction between accepting political responsibility and being directly culpable. In Hong Kong, Chief Executive John Lee and seven senior officials apologised over the Wang Fuk Court fire in Tai Po, which killed 168...

title: Paleontologists Still Argue Over Whether Spinosaurus Was a Swimmer or a Wader — and Each New Fossil Changes the Answer
UN climate chief urges speed as COP31 confronts fossil fuel divide
description: ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 14 (Reuters) - The UN's top climate official urged negotiators at the COP31 conference in Turkey on Saturday to move swiftly towards a deal and "avoid tactical delays" as the summit heads into its second and final week.

title: What Is An Ocarina? The Ancient History Behind the 'Legend of Zelda’ Instrument
description: Ocarinas date back thousands of years, and were used in Mesoamerican rituals and ceremonies. Yet they were on the verge of obscurity before 'Legend of Zelda.'

title: Ancient Earthen Mounds Still Rise Above The Farmland At This Overlooked Missouri Historic Site
description: A 16-foot temple mound, built by hand one basket of dirt at a time, still stands in the middle of farm country. Nobody even knows what its builders called
